vulnerabilities.name: Reflected Origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin
vulnerabilities.description: Server echoes the request's Origin header back verbatim as Access-Control-Allow-Origin instead of validating it against an allow-list, letting any origin read cross-origin responses.
vulnerabilities.notes: Confirmed when Access-Control-Allow-Origin in the response exactly equals the Origin value sent in the request, including for arbitrary/attacker-controlled origins.

vulnerabilities.name: Wildcard ACAO Combined with Credentials
vulnerabilities.description: Response sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Per spec browsers should reject this combination, but misconfigurations (dynamic wildcard generation, proxy rewriting) can still expose credentialed data.
vulnerabilities.notes: Also check for ACAO dynamically generated as "*" per-origin (effectively a wildcard) rather than a literal static header.

vulnerabilities.name: Null Origin Allow-Listed
vulnerabilities.description: Server accepts Origin: null as valid, which can be forced by an attacker via a sandboxed iframe, a data: URI, or a file:// context, bypassing normal origin restrictions.

vulnerabilities.name: Weak Origin Suffix/Substring Matching
vulnerabilities.description: Server validates Origin by substring/suffix check (e.g. endswith "example.com") instead of exact domain match, so an attacker-registered domain like evilexample.com or example.com.attacker.com satisfies the check.
vulnerabilities.notes: Confirmed by observing ACAO reflect an origin that merely contains the trusted domain as a substring rather than matching it exactly.

vulnerabilities.name: Weak Origin Prefix Matching
vulnerabilities.description: Server validates Origin by prefix check (e.g. startswith "https://trusted.com") without a following delimiter, so https://trusted.com.attacker.com or https://trusted.comattacker.com passes validation.

vulnerabilities.name: Insecure Regex-Based Origin Allow-List
vulnerabilities.description: Server allow-lists origins via a regular expression with unescaped special characters (e.g. an unescaped dot matching any character), allowing lookalike domains to pass validation.
vulnerabilities.notes: Differential testing: compare ACAO behavior for the real domain vs. a lookalike (one character substituted, or a dot replaced with another character) to detect loose regex matching.

vulnerabilities.name: Sensitive Endpoint Lacks Vary: Origin
vulnerabilities.description: A dynamically-reflected ACAO response is cached by an intermediary without Vary: Origin, so a response generated for one origin can be served to a different, unintended origin from cache.
vulnerabilities.notes: Combine with web_cache.json findings: if the endpoint is also behind a shared cache, this compounds into cross-user CORS response poisoning.

vulnerabilities.name: Overly Permissive Access-Control-Allow-Headers / Methods
vulnerabilities.description: Preflight response allows a wildcard or an unnecessarily broad set of methods/headers (e.g. Authorization, X-Api-Key) for cross-origin requests, widening the attack surface for any origin that is otherwise allow-listed.

vulnerabilities.name: Trusted Internal/Staging Origin Exposed
vulnerabilities.description: Allow-list includes internal, staging, or localhost origins (e.g. http://localhost, http://127.0.0.1, internal dev domains) that remain reachable from a public-facing production endpoint.

vulnerabilities.name: Missing Access-Control-Allow-Credentials Check on Sensitive Data Endpoint
vulnerabilities.description: An endpoint returning session- or user-specific data sets a permissive ACAO without requiring Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, relying on client-side assumptions; some clients/libraries still forward cookies via fetch(..., {credentials: 'include'}) regardless, exposing data if ACAO is reflected.
